notes: Extends the SIM-aware attach-APN self-heal to the Telit ECM data path. A recycled or SIM-swapped Telit that carried a stale CGDCONT CID1 APN from a prior deployment (e.g. internet.cxn now paired with a Kore SIM) bound ECM to the wrong APN and stayed dark through every reboot — the Telit mirror of the Quectel cause-55/33 trap. ctt-modem-provision rolls to 0.3.3; the fleet pin picks it up on the next OTA.
bugs: A recycled or SIM-swapped Telit no longer strands on a stale attach APN (ctt-modem-provision 0.3.3). The Telit ECM provisioner returned as soon as the ECM session was bound and never checked the attach context, so a Telit carrying a wrong CGDCONT CID1 from a prior deployment (internet.cxn baked in, now with a Kore SIM) bound ECM to the wrong APN and the PDN stayed dead through every reboot — the Telit-side mirror of the Quectel cause-55/33 trap. The provisioner now runs the shared attach-APN heal after the ECM bind for both modem families: read CGDCONT CID1, rewrite a non-blank wrong APN via CFUN=0/CGDCONT/CFUN=1, and publish the dial APN, keyed on the SIM IMSI home PLMN with a hardened ICCID issuer-prefix fallback. The carrier/APN logic and rewrite routine move into the base Modem class; modem AT commands are split into at::/at::quectel::/at::telit:: namespaces. Hardware-verified on a Telit: a bad context survived a 0.3.2 boot and 0.3.3 healed it (internet.cxn to super) at boot before ModemManager. The fleet pin system/native/ctt-modem-provision.version rolls to 0.3.3.

notes: Cellular integrity and boot-sequence finalization for the lts_26_07 image. The Quectel dial/attach APN is now chosen from the SIM's IMSI home PLMN (Telenor 24008) instead of the ICCID country code — a Telenor SIM in an 8901 (US-numbered) ICCID range had been assigned 'super' and refused by the network with 3GPP cause 33. OTA no longer clobbers a Quectel's autoconnect, the modem retries forever and cannot steal the default route, and the application layer is now OTA-self-enabling with corrected startup ordering. ctt-modem-provision rolls to 0.3.2.
features: collect-diagnostics is now an on-station CLI (/usr/local/sbin/collect-diagnostics): system/scripts/collect-diagnostics.sh gathers a read-only bundle (identity, hardware, services, modem plus SIM ICCID/IMSI, and logs) as the ctt user with no sudo and prints the tarball path. Single source of truth for what a diagnostic bundle contains; the client-side SSH wrappers become thin invokers.

User-facing CLI symlinks are now created by an OTA hook (install-scripts.sh), not only by the Ansible image build: station-id, program-radios, program-radio, update-station, bash-update-station, upload-station-data and collect-diagnostics are symlinked into /usr/local/sbin, so an OTA self-heals a lost symlink and an image built without the Ansible role still ships its CLIs. Runs in image-bake mode too.

ctt-modem-provision built, tagged (ctt-modem-provision-v0.3.2) and published (armhf binary + sha256); the fleet pin system/native/ctt-modem-provision.version is rolled to 0.3.2, so stations pick it up on the next OTA.

All modem AT-command strings are centralized in native/lib/ctthw/modem/at_commands.h (named constants + a cgdcontDefine builder), replacing inline literals across the Quectel, Telit, and modem-detect drivers.
bugs: Quectel APN is selected from the SIM's IMSI home PLMN (AT+CIMI; MCC 240 / MNC 08 = Telenor Connexion), not the ICCID country code. Telenor also ships SIMs in an 8901 (US-numbered) ICCID range whose country code reads 01, so the old rule assigned 'super' and the network refused the data bearer with 3GPP cause 33 (option-unsubscribed): registered with good signal but no traffic, re-broken on every boot. A hardened ICCID issuer-prefix match (8946 or 890124008) is kept as a fallback for modems that will not report an IMSI. Found on V2 station F5C51E6B6AFA and corroborated by the Telenor subscription-activity log; hardware-verified end-to-end (break CID1 to super, reboot, boot guard recovers to internet.cxn by IMSI).

ICCID fallback hardened to the Telenor issuer prefix. When no IMSI is available, APN selection matches an ICCID starting 8946 or 890124008 (8901 plus the embedded Telenor PLMN 24008), not the 2-digit country code. Bare 8901 is a broad US range: fleet-validated against 7858 Telenor and 2792 Kore ICCIDs, 964 Kore SIMs start 8901 and would have been mis-routed to internet.cxn; 890124008 is Telenor-exclusive. Zero misclassification across the full fleet.

OTA no longer clobbers a Quectel's autoconnect. deploy_dir copied the station-modem profile wholesale and only stripped runtime-owned keys from the diff, so the repo's autoconnect=false overwrote the live value on any redeploy. It bit only Quectel because NetworkManager omits autoconnect=true (its default) from the keyfile. deploy_dir now reads an absent preserved key as the daemon default and omits it (never falling back to the source value), and install-network.sh re-runs modem-datapath.sh after the deploy to re-assert the per-modem policy. Verified on real NM 1.30.6 and on hardware.

station-modem retries forever instead of surrendering after four attempts: autoconnect-retries is pinned to 0 (non-default, so it is written to the keyfile and survives an install-network redeploy). Cellular can no longer steal the default route: ipv4.route-metric is pinned to 700.

Application layer is now OTA-self-enabling and correctly ordered. install-systemd.sh MUST_BE_ENABLED now covers the Node and SensorGnome units (previously deployed as files but enabled only by Ansible/manufacturing, so a lost symlink or an Ansible-free image came up with no application layer). sensorgnome.service orders After=ctt-board-detect.service bootcount.service, the two units that produce its synchronous inputs /etc/ctt/station-id and /etc/bootcount, fixing a stale premise and a race on bootcount. The four long-running station-* services get StartLimitIntervalSec=0 and RestartSec=5, so a transient boot-time crash-loop retries forever instead of hitting systemd's default 5-starts-in-10s give-up and leaving a headless station dark.

notes: Makes the front-panel IP Address screen show USB-ethernet dongles that do not enumerate as eth*.
bugs: The LCD Ip Address screen showed a blank address for a USB-ethernet dongle that enumerates under a name other than eth* (a predictable name such as enx<mac>, or the legacy usb0), because the interface filter matched only eth* and wlan*. It now also matches enx* and usb0, anchored so virtual interfaces such as veth* that merely contain 'eth' are excluded, and long enx names are shown on their own row before the address. The modem point-to-point NAT (mdm0, 192.168.225.x) and ppp0 stay off the screen because they are not reachable addresses (PR #48).

notes: Fixes the image bake so native binaries actually land in built images, completes the Telit RNDIS-to-ECM conversion within a single boot, and hardens the BluSeries/radio driver against an unplugged receiver. Pins ctt-modem-provision 0.3.1 fleet-wide and stamps the image build date.
features: ctt-modem-provision is pinned to 0.3.1 across the fleet.

/etc/ctt/station-image is now stamped with the image build date at CI build time, distinct from /etc/ctt/station-software, which records the last software-update time on every update-station run (build and OTA).
bugs: Native binaries now actually land in built images. install-native.sh verified each fetched armhf binary by running it for --version, which cannot execute under the image build's qemu-arm emulation, so the check failed and the install was silently skipped, publishing images with no native binaries (modem provisioner, radio/blu drivers, board-detect). In build mode the tool now trusts the checksum and pin and skips the exec smoke test, and the build fails loudly if a deploy hook errors. A second silent failure, nmcli connection reload hard-failing in the chroot with no NetworkManager D-Bus, is fixed by skipping runtime NM/udev reloads in build mode; the configs apply on first boot (PRs #44, #46).

Telit LE910Q1 RNDIS-to-CDC-ECM conversion now completes in a single boot (ctt-modem-provision 0.3.0 to 0.3.1). A fresh or replacement Telit previously needed two reboots to converge, leaving mdm0 down (no cellular) in between. The provisioner now waits for the modem to re-enumerate as ECM within the same boot, reopens the AT port, and completes the bind (AT#ECM=1,0), running Before=ModemManager so the wait is uncontended, and fails open to the previous two-boot behavior if the port does not return in time.

The BluSeries and 434-radio driver template units no longer fail-loop when their USB device is unplugged. They set StartLimitIntervalSec=0 (never give up) but had only an ordering dependency on the device, so unplugging a receiver left the instance restarting every 2 s forever. Added BindsTo the .device unit so systemd stops the instance on removal (udev restarts it on re-attach), plus ConditionPathExists against the unplug/settle race. Retry-forever for a present-but-glitching receiver is preserved.

BluSeries detections poll no longer throws TypeError reading 'forEach' when a receiver stops responding. A timed-out poll delivers data undefined; blu-base-station.js now guards Array.isArray before iterating, mirroring the existing VERSION-task guard.

notes: Extends the native modem provisioner to the Quectel EC25 so its LTE attach APN cannot diverge from the dial APN (the 3GPP cause 55 'registered but no data' failure), unifies the dial-APN source, and requests an IPv4-only bearer for IPv4-only M2M SIMs.
features: Native cellular modem provisioner extended to the Quectel EC25 (ctt-modem-provision 0.2.0 to 0.3.0). Provisioning is refactored into a small unit-tested ctthw/modem C++ module, an AT-port transport with one driver per modem family. For a Quectel it keeps the LTE attach APN (CGDCONT CID1) matched to the SIM so it cannot diverge from the NetworkManager dial APN, a divergence the network rejects with 3GPP cause 55, leaving the modem registered but passing no data. It reads the SIM ICCID (AT+QCCID) and, only when CID1 carries a non-empty wrong APN, rewrites it (CFUN=0 / CGDCONT=1,'IP',<apn> / CFUN=1); a blank CID1 is left alone. Runs Before=ModemManager, idempotent and fail-open, so a stale or recycled attach context self-heals on the next boot. Verified against the Quectel AT Commands Manual V2.0 and on hardware. The Telit LE910Q1 ECM data-path provisioning is unchanged.

check-sim-id.sh renamed to provision-modem-apn.sh and reworked to consume /run/ctt/modem-apn (written by the native provisioner) as the single source for the dial APN, so the attach APN and the dial APN share one origin and cannot diverge; the previous mmcli-ICCID mapping is kept as a fallback.
New udev symlink /dev/ctt-modem-at for the Quectel EC25 AT control port (interface 02).
The native-tool release workflow now publishes formatted Markdown release notes.
bugs: The modem now requests IPv4-only. These M2M SIMs and APNs are provisioned IPv4-only, so a dual-stack (IPv4v6) bearer request made the modem attempt an IPv6 PDN the network refused (QMI CallFailed / ip-version-mismatch). Sets ipv6.method=disabled on the station-modem profile (gsm.ip-type is not usable on NetworkManager 1.30 / Bullseye).
First-time SensorGnome tag-database upload no longer fails when there is no existing SG_tag_database file to remove (rm -f).

notes: Fixes SensorGnome tag-database uploads through the station web interface.
bugs: SensorGnome tag-database uploads now persist. The /upload-sg-tag-file handler called fs.writeFileSync() but never imported fs, so every upload threw ReferenceError: fs is not defined after it had already removed the existing SG_tag_database* file. Uploading a tag database therefore deleted the current one and wrote nothing, leaving an empty/missing SG_tag_database.sqlite and causing the SensorGnome interface to fail with 'no such table: tags'. Adds the missing import fs from 'fs' (PR #40).

notes: Two hardware-validated fixes for a fresh test image. (1) The cellular modem can now actually be disabled on ECM-mode Telit units (1bc7:7021). (2) Radio MCUs that have only a bootloader (a blank/erased Feather 32u4, USB 239a:000c) can now be flashed, and radio flashing is now a pure-shell script (an stty 1200-baud touch plus avrdude; the former native ctt-radio-flash tool is removed). Also restores the station-hardware-server /sensor route.
bugs: Disabling the cellular modem now actually disables it on ECM-mode Telit units (1bc7:7021, CDC-ECM). modem-power.sh and modem-boot-state.sh matched only the RNDIS PID 1bc7:7020, so disable wrote the intent marker but never deauthorized the device: it stayed authorized, ModemManager kept the modem, cellular kept passing traffic, and a disabled modem came back fully on after a reboot. Both scripts now match 7021 and 7020 (as enable-modem/modem-wake/modem-datapath already did). Hardware-validated: disable sets authorized=0 and ModemManager drops it; disable plus reboot stays off.
station-hardware-server /sensor returned 404 because the root route was missing; re-added to serve /run/ctt/sensors.json.

Flash radio MCUs that are in bootloader-only mode (no app firmware). A blank/erased Feather 32u4 enumerates as USB 239a:000c instead of the app's 239a:800c; the radio udev rule matched 800c only, so a bootloader-mode board never got a /dev/ctt-radio/chN symlink (program-radios could not discover it) and the 1200-baud touch waited forever for a disconnect that never comes. udev now emits three rules per channel: a PID-agnostic identity symlink (the physical port is the channel, in app or bootloader mode), a CTT_RADIO_MODE=app|bootloader property, and the per-channel driver launch gated on the app PID (so a board dropping to the bootloader mid-flash never relaunches the driver and avrdude keeps the port). program-radio.sh reads the mode and either does the 1200-baud touch (app board) or flashes directly (bootloader board). Radio flashing is now pure shell (stty touch + avrdude); the native ctt-radio-flash tool is removed. Validated on a V3 station.

notes: Replaces 2.2.1's first-boot resize mechanism, which did not complete on the CM3+ station image. Station software is otherwise functionally identical to 2.2.0/2.2.1.
bugs: First-boot rootfs expansion now completes. 2.2.1 restored the stock init_resize cmdline hook, but on the CTT image its two-stage reboot dance (grow partition, reboot, resize2fs_once grows the fs) never finished the filesystem grow, so stations still booted ~96% full. 2.2.2 strips init_resize from cmdline.txt and hands expansion to ctt-firstboot-resize.service: fail-safe (a normal oneshot after the OS is up, not PID 1), stateless (decides purely from on-disk geometry with no marker, so a QAQC-booted base image cannot disable it and it self-heals), and one-pass with no reboot (grows the partition via sfdisk --no-reread -N + partx -u and the filesystem via resize2fs, using only base-image tools). Validated end-to-end on a fresh CM3+ eMMC flash.

notes: Image-pipeline fixes so CI-built images burn fast, plus a license-metadata correction (package.json/README set to AGPL-3.0-or-later to match LICENSE.txt). Station software is functionally identical to 2.2.0. Note: 2.2.1's first-boot resize approach was superseded by 2.2.2.
bugs: Images burned ~3x too slowly: arm-runner's optimize_image zeroed free space but never truncated the padded image, so each CI image shipped ~6 GiB uncompressed. The build now runs PiShrink (-s, truncate only) and purges apt/npm/log caches before shrinking (~6.3 GiB to ~3.6 GiB).

notes: Migrates the Telit LE910Q1 cellular data path from RNDIS to CDC-ECM and makes modem provisioning zero-touch at boot. RNDIS is deprecated in the Linux kernel and is not manageable by ModemManager; ECM is standards-based and yields a clean, MM-visible mdm0 path. A modem is provisioned once (the NV state persists), and if a fresh/replacement modem is fitted an idempotent boot guard converts it automatically. Hardware-validated from ECM-provisioned, RNDIS-provisioned, and factory (unbound) starting states.
features: ctt-modem-provision.service: idempotent ECM boot guard. Runs Before=ModemManager for exclusive AT-port access (no MM/NM shutdown, so none of the old provisioner races). Read-only no-op on an already-provisioned modem; converts a fresh/swapped RNDIS modem to ECM over two boots (AT#USBCFG=1 + reboot, then AT#ECM=1,0); re-asserts a lost bind. Fails open, never blocks boot.

ctt-modem-ecm-up.service + modem-ecm-up.sh: ECM data-path bring-up. NetworkManager folds the ECM net port into the ModemManager modem and never DHCPs mdm0, so it is brought up out of band via dhclient (the module serves 192.168.225.1 and leases .2), then the default route is re-pinned to a high fallback metric (700) so cellular never preempts wired/Wi-Fi.

Telit data path migrated RNDIS to CDC-ECM: ctt-modem-provision 0.2.0 provisions ECM and migrates existing RNDIS units; udev rules dual-recognize 1bc7:7021 (ECM) alongside 1bc7:7020 (RNDIS, transitional) and rename the net device to mdm0.
systemd units invoke their scripts via /bin/bash <script> instead of relying on the file executable bit, which does not survive Git reliably on Windows.
bugs: Fix ctt-modem-ecm-up.service failing 203/EXEC because modem-ecm-up.sh was committed non-executable, so the data interface never came up on a clean deploy.

Fix the ECM boot guard being deleted immediately after install: ctt-modem-provision.service was still listed in the systemd REMOVED manifest from when the RNDIS auto-provisioner was retired, so the OTA installed the guard and then removed it.

notes: CI/image-pipeline release: release tags now build immutable, versioned images.
features: build-image auto-builds on a release-tag push (v*.*.*) and serializes builds. Each build publishes an immutable, version-named artifact (sensor-station-v<version>.img.xz) rather than a bare-date name, and cuts a GitHub pre-release pointing at it. The lts_26_07 image line is isolated under images/lts_26_07/ so it never touches the current public LTS.

notes: Cellular modem robustness and the incremental CI image build.
features: ctt-modem-wake.service: modem power-state recovery at boot. A Telit LE910Q1 in ON_OFF# shutdown (after a hard reset / VBAT loss) does not self-enumerate; this pulses ON_OFF# so it returns before ModemManager scans. No-op when the modem is already present or intent is OFF.
Incremental CI image build (build-image): loop-mounts the previous image under qemu-arm and runs update-station.sh inside it, then shrinks and publishes to S3 - the manual image process, automated.
bugs: Fix web-triggered update-station killing itself: the dashboard spawns the updater inside station-radio-interface; restarting that service mid-run SIGKILLed the updater. The radio-interface restart is now the last action, and the updater runs in a decoupled transient unit.

notes: Bug-fix release on top of 2.0.0: two fixes that restore the station internal control plane and the OTA update path on the Node 20 image. (Never tagged as a standalone release; shipped as part of the first 2.x tag, v2.1.0.)
bugs: Fix internal HTTP over localhost resolving to IPv6 (::1): Node services reach station-hardware-server at http://localhost:3000, which binds IPv4-only (127.0.0.1). On Node 20 localhost resolves to ::1 first and node-fetch connects to that single address with no fallback, so every internal call failed with ECONNREFUSED ::1:3000. Each service now forces IPv4-first DNS ordering; external resolution is unchanged.

Fix update-station failing when launched from the web dashboard: the button spawns the script from a root service with no $HOME, so git config --global failed and the dubious-ownership guard aborted the pull. The script now sets $HOME when unset and injects safe.directory via the environment.

notes: The first 2.x: a native hardware/radio layer and a new LTS image path. Moves hardware bring-up and direct device I/O out of the Node app into small compiled C++ tools started by systemd/udev; Node services become consumers of stable /run/ctt/ file and socket contracts. Drivers ship as versioned, prebuilt armhf binaries fetched over OTA - stations never compile. Major, breaking change to the on-device architecture. (Never tagged standalone; shipped as part of the first 2.x tag, v2.1.0.)
features: ctthw C++ hardware library: one driver class per chip (I/O expander, ADC, temperature, RTC, board-ID EEPROM, character LCD) over a single /dev/i2c-1 wrapper with cross-process bus locking. Shared by all native tools.

Native device tools: ctt-board-detect (board identity to /run/ctt/board.env), ctt-radio-driver@N and ctt-blu-driver@N (receiver serial to sockets), ctt-sensors (ADC+temp to /run/ctt/sensors.json, covering V3 MAX11645+TMP411 and V2 ADS7924+TMP102), ctt-leds (V3 status LEDs), ctt-lcd (character LCD), ctt-radio-flash (GPIO-free radio firmware flashing).
Front-panel LCD status: boot splash, shutdown indicator, an 'Updating...' splash held for the duration of an OTA, and a radio-fault banner when the radio service is down.
Kernel gpio-keys front-panel buttons via a board-gated device-tree overlay; the LCD menu reads evdev key events instead of polling GPIO in-process.
ctt-device-config applies one canonical per-board-revision /boot/config.txt (copy + reboot-once with a hash-keyed loop breaker), replacing the dynamic boot-overlay services.
OTA native-binary delivery: CI publishes a versioned, checksummed armhf binary per tool; the OTA hook fetches and verifies the fleet-pinned version (system/native/). Per-tool versioning, no lockstep.
system/migrations/ for live in-place field-station upgrades (safe by default, requires --force); reflashing the prepared image remains the recommended upgrade.

station-radio-interface consumes the ctt-radio-driver/ctt-blu-driver sockets instead of opening serial ports directly; station-hardware-server /sensor reads /run/ctt/sensors.json; Node services launch directly via node for clean SIGTERM; OS configuration consolidated into system/; ctt-sensors steady-state logging cut ~60x (heartbeat + transitions).
bugs: OTA durability: update-station now syncs after the pull and after the deploy hooks, so a hard power-off seconds after an update can no longer zero the freshly written files (ext4 ordered-mode writeback). The pull is hardened (--ff-only, retry, abort-on-failure).
Cellular: stations no longer auto-dial PPP on the newer modem; migrated images ship with the modem off until enabled.
WiFi reachability: disable NetworkManager WiFi power-save via a global conf.d drop-in, so a WiFi-connected station no longer sleeps and stops answering ARP.

WiFi-from-USB (/usb/wifi): await the nmcli connect before the follow-up config command and handle failures, so a failed join returns an error instead of an unhandled rejection that crashed station-hardware-server.
LCD: native re-initialization recovers a warm controller from any state (no more garbled output on a service restart); fixed a menu back-navigation crash.
station-radio-interface: guard a null data-receiver result during line parsing.
Boot: removed a deadlock path so SIM/APN selection no longer blocks modem startup.

notes: Telit LE910Q1 cellular support and OTA modernization. Migrates the cellular data path from Quectel EC25 (QMI+PPP) to Telit LE910Q1 (RNDIS, mdm0 interface). Introduces a modular OTA hook system so future deployment changes ship without touching update-station.sh. Modernizes the /modem API so the LCD, web UI, and check-ins share one cached mmcli poller instead of each forking subprocesses.
features: Telit LE910Q1-WWG modem support end to end (enable/disable, udev, NetworkManager profiles); cellular data path switches from PPP to RNDIS using the modem's mdm0 netdev.

Modular OTA hook system: post-merge.sh orchestrator iterates post-merge.d/ drop-ins (install-systemd, install-udev, install-network). Adding a new subsystem deploy is now a single file drop, not an update-station.sh edit.
Pre-merge OTA hook orchestrator wired in as a placeholder phase for future pre-pull tasks.
Adaptive /modem cache in hardware-server: one background mmcli poll loop serves all consumers, polls every 2 s while active, idle after 60 s, exposes real RSRP / RSRQ / SNR via mmcli --signal-setup.
Connectivity probe for /modem/ppp: actual ping through the modem interface every 10 s while active, replacing the old 'any modem interface exists' check that misled the LED on unprovisioned modems.
Modem boot-state persistence: operator on/off intent survives hard reboots via a marker file (modem-boot-state.service).
IMEI-gated boot-time RNDIS NV provisioner for Telit modems; subsequently moved to manufacturing.
sensorgnome.service and bootcount.service brought under monorepo + OTA control; boottime_compute.sh moves into system/scripts/.
78-ctt-radios.rules: positive-filter radio identification by USB VID:PID via udev (replaces fragile by-path substring matching).
tools/modem-snapshot.sh: read-only diagnostic dump capturing mmcli / ip / dmesg state for support escalations.
Wired uplink default-route metric pinned below cellular so eth0 wins when both interfaces are present.
list-devices.sh extended to recognize the new Telit modem.
bugs: Fix boot deadlock where check-sim-id started ModemManager too early, before the SIM was ready.

Fix LCD modem signal showing ':!' for working RNDIS modems; the old state check required state=='connected' but ModemManager never advances past 'registered' on the RNDIS path. Accepts more states plus requires a numeric signal value.
Fix /modem/ppp false positives on unprovisioned modems whose mdm0 came up without LTE forwarding (LED stayed on with no real connectivity).
Fix sensorgnome.service first-boot ENOENT race against /etc/ctt/station-id by adding After=station-boot.service.
Fix FunCube USB endpoints crowding the bus: 77-ctt-telit-block-unused.rules now also blocks Telit interfaces 06 / 07.
Fix missing executable bit on modem-boot-state.sh.
removed: Automatic station reboot at the end of update-station.sh; reboots are now operator-driven.
provision-modem.service (CGDCONT cleanup, PPP era) — replaced by the RNDIS data path.
provision-modem-rndis.service and boot-time RNDIS NV provisioning — moved to manufacturing; stations now assume the modem ships pre-provisioned.
